_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 11 Physical Sciences P2 (Chemistry), November 2024 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper2.pdf, paper2_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. The guideline is
bilingual (English/Afrikaans); only the English is transcribed. memo_answer gives the guideline's
working and final answers (tick marks removed); diagrams, graphs and circuits are described in
brackets in the question text. Data sheets printed with the paper are not transcribed.
FORMAT: 150 marks, 3 hours, eight compulsory questions (Q1 multiple choice 20 marks).

subject: Physical Sciences

questions.context: QUESTION 1: MULTIPLE-CHOICE QUESTIONS. Various options are provided as possible answers to the following questions. Choose the answer and write only the letter (A-D) next to the question numbers (1.1 to 1.10) in the ANSWER BOOK, for example 1.11 D.
questions.text: Which ONE of the following bonds will have the highest bond energy? A H – H B C – H C C = C D C ≡ C
questions.topic: Atomic combinations: bonding, molecular shapes and polarity
questions.memo_answer: D

questions.text: Consider the following compounds and their respective boiling points: He -268,9 °C; HBr -66 °C; HF 19,5 °C. The correct arrangement for the decreasing strength of the intermolecular forces of the given compounds is ... A HF, He, HBr. B HBr, He, HF. C HF, HBr, He. D He, HBr, HF.
questions.topic: Intermolecular forces and physical properties
questions.memo_answer: C

questions.text: Which ONE of the following is NOT a property of the ideal gas? A There are no forces of attraction between the molecules. B The collisions between molecules are elastic. C The volume occupied by the gas is equal to the total volume of the gas molecules. D It has a low density.
questions.topic: Ideal gases and the gas laws
questions.memo_answer: C

questions.text: The molar mass of hydrated oxalic acid (COOH)2·xH2O is 126 g·mol⁻¹. The number of water molecules (x) present in the hydrated compound is ... A 1. B 2. C 3. D 4.

questions.memo_answer: B

questions.text: Consider the potential energy versus distance curve below. questions.text: Will I2 be soluble in CCℓ4? Write down only YES or NO.

questions.text: Explain the answer to QUESTION 2.6 by referring to the molecular polarity and intermolecular forces involved in the compounds.
questions.topic: Intermolecular forces and physical properties
questions.memo_answer:
I2 is a non-polar molecule and only contains London forces.
CCℓ4 is a non-polar molecule and only contains London forces.
Both compounds are non-polar and only have London forces and "like dissolves like".

questions.context: 2.8 The following table shows the average bond energies of atoms that are bonded to the hydrogen atom. [C-H 413 kJ·mol⁻¹; O-H 463 kJ·mol⁻¹; F-H 565 kJ·mol⁻¹]
questions.text: Define the term bond energy.
questions.topic: Atomic combinations: bonding, molecular shapes and polarity
questions.memo_answer: Bond energy is the energy needed to break one mole of its molecules into separate atoms.

questions.text: Explain the trend observed in the bond energy in the table above.
questions.topic: Atomic combinations: bonding, molecular shapes and polarity
questions.memo_answer:
The atomic size decreases in the period (from C to F).
The bond length decreases from C to F.
The shorter the bond length the more energy is needed to break the bond.

questions.context: QUESTION 3 (Start on a new page.) Learners investigated the boiling points of the compounds listed in the table below. [A CH4 -161,5 °C; B SiH4 -111,8 °C; C GeH4 -88,6 °C; D SnH4 -52 °C]
questions.text: Define boiling point.
questions.topic: Intermolecular forces and physical properties
questions.memo_answer: The temperature at which the vapour pressure of a substance equals atmospheric pressure.

questions.text: Is this a fair investigation? Write only YES or NO. Give a reason for the answer.
questions.topic: Intermolecular forces and physical properties
questions.memo_answer:
YES
Only one independent variable / all variables are controlled except molecular mass.

questions.text: Write down the phase of the above compounds at room temperature.
questions.topic: Intermolecular forces and physical properties
questions.memo_answer: Gas

questions.text: Explain the trend observed in boiling points of the compounds in the table above by referring to the molecular mass, intermolecular forces, and energy involved.
questions.topic: Intermolecular forces and physical properties
questions.memo_answer:
• The molecular mass increases from A to D
• The strength of the London forces increases with an increase in the molecular size/mass.
• More energy will be required to overcome the intermolecular forces from A to D
OR
• The molecular mass decreases from D to A
• The strength of the London forces decreases with decrease in molecular size/mass.
• Less energy will be required to overcome the intermolecular forces from D to A

questions.text: Which compound in the table above has the highest vapour pressure at a given temperature? Explain the answer by referring to the data in the table above.
questions.topic: Intermolecular forces and physical properties
questions.memo_answer:
Compound A (CH4)
It has the lowest boiling point.

questions.context: 3.6 The boiling point of HF and HCℓ is compared. [E HF 19,5 °C; F HCℓ X]
questions.text: Will the value of X be HIGHER THAN, LOWER THAN or EQUAL TO 19,5 °C?
questions.topic: Intermolecular forces and physical properties
questions.memo_answer: Lower than

questions.text: Fully explain the answer to QUESTION 3.6.1.
questions.topic: Intermolecular forces and physical properties
questions.memo_answer:
• HF has hydrogen bonds.
• HCℓ has dipole-dipole forces.
• Hydrogen bonds are stronger than dipole-dipole forces.
• More energy is needed to overcome the intermolecular forces in HF.
OR
• HF has hydrogen bonds; HCℓ has dipole-dipole forces; dipole-dipole forces are weaker than hydrogen bonds; less energy is needed to overcome the intermolecular forces in HCℓ.

questions.context: QUESTION 4 (Start on a new page.) Learners investigated the relationship between pressure and volume of a gas. The graph below shows the results obtained during the investigation. [Graph PRESSURE VS VOLUME: volume (cm³, 0-20) against pressure (x 10³ Pa, 0-180); a decreasing curve through points near (30; 18), (35; 15), (45; 10), (82; 6) and (165; 3).]
questions.text: Name and state the law the experiment is based on.
questions.topic: Ideal gases and the gas laws
questions.memo_answer:
Boyle's law
The pressure of an enclosed gas is inversely proportional to the volume it occupies at constant temperature.

questions.text: Write down a hypothesis for this investigation.
questions.topic: Ideal gases and the gas laws
questions.memo_answer:
Criteria: the independent and dependent variables are stated correctly; a statement about the relationship between the independent and dependent variables.
The higher the pressure of a gas the lower its volume.

questions.text: Read and write down the pressure from the graph when the volume is 12 cm3.
questions.topic: Ideal gases and the gas laws
questions.memo_answer: 40 x 10³ Pa / 4 kPa
questions.memo_note: The alternative "4 kPa" printed in the guideline is a slip: 40 x 10³ Pa = 40 kPa.

questions.text: Calculate the volume at 200 kPa.
questions.topic: Ideal gases and the gas laws
questions.memo_answer:
p1V1 = p2V2
(40 x 10³)(12) = (200 x 10³)V2
V2 = 2,4 cm³
(Use any correct co-ordinates from the graph.)

questions.text: Redraw the above graph and label it A. On the same set of axes draw the graph to show how a real gas will deviate at a high pressure. Label this graph as B.
questions.topic: Ideal gases and the gas laws
questions.memo_answer:
Graph A (the given curve) redrawn; graph B (real gas) drawn as a dashed curve that lies higher than A at high pressure (volume larger than ideal).

questions.context: QUESTION 5 (Start on a new page.) Consider the decomposition reaction of dinitrogen pentoxide: 2 N2O5(g) → 2 N2O4(g) + O2(g). The table below shows the different energies for the above reaction. [Heat of the reactants (Hr) 26,6 kJ·mol⁻¹; activation energy (Ea) 6,73 kJ·mol⁻¹; heat of the reaction (ΔH) -7,28 kJ·mol⁻¹]
questions.text: Define the term activation energy.
questions.topic: Energy and chemical change
questions.memo_answer: The minimum energy needed for a reaction to take place.

questions.text: Is the above reaction ENDOTHERMIC or EXOTHERMIC? Give a reason for the answer.
questions.topic: Energy and chemical change
questions.memo_answer:
Exothermic
ΔH < 0

questions.text: Calculate the heat of the products.
questions.topic: Energy and chemical change
questions.memo_answer:
ΔH = Hp - Hr
-7,28 = Hp - 26,6
Hp = 19,32 kJ·mol⁻¹

questions.text: Draw the potential energy versus course of reaction graph for the above reaction. On the graph indicate values for: • Heat of reactants (Hreactants) • Heat of products (Hproducts) • Energy at the activated complex • Heat of the reaction (ΔH)
questions.topic: Energy and chemical change
questions.memo_answer:
Exothermic potential energy curve: reactants at 26,6 kJ·mol⁻¹; peak (activated complex) at 33,33 kJ·mol⁻¹; products at 19,32 kJ·mol⁻¹; ΔH shown as the drop from reactants to products.
Marking: Hr correct; Hp correct; ΔH correct; energy at the activated complex; correct shape.
NOTE: if an endothermic curve is drawn, maximum 2/5.
questions.memo_note: The guideline sketch labels ΔH as -25 kJ·mol⁻¹; from the data ΔH = 19,32 - 26,6 = -7,28 kJ·mol⁻¹.

questions.text: On the same graph drawn in QUESTION 5.4, use a dotted line and draw the shape of the graph when a catalyst is added to the original reaction.
questions.topic: Energy and chemical change
questions.memo_answer:
Dotted curve on the same axes, starting at the reactant energy and ending at the product energy, with a lower peak.
Marking: curve starts at the initial potential energy of the reactants and ends at the final potential energy of the products; curve peak is lower.

questions.context: QUESTION 6 (Start on a new page.) 6.1 Compound Q (CxHy) reacts with oxygen according to the balanced equation: P CxHy + 13 O2 → 8 CO2 + 10 H2O. The molar mass of compound Q is 58 g·mol⁻¹.

questions.memo_answer: The simplest whole number ratio of atoms in a compound.

questions.topic: Quantitative aspects: moles, molar volume and concentration

questions.context: The percentage composition of compound Q is: carbon 82,76%; hydrogen 17,24%.
questions.text: Determine the molecular formula of compound Q.
questions.topic: Quantitative aspects: moles, molar volume and concentration
questions.memo_answer:
OPTION 1 (percentage composition):
mol C : mol H = 82,76/12 : 17,24/1 = 6,90 : 17,24 = 1 : 2,5 = 2 : 5
Empirical formula: C2H5; formula mass = 2(12) + 5(1) = 29
Ratio = 58 / 29 = 2
Molecular formula: C4H10
OPTION 2 (conservation of atoms): 2 C = 8 C, C = 4; 2 H = 10 H2, H = (10)(2)/2 = 10
Molecular formula: C4H10

questions.context: QUESTION 7 (Start on a new page.) 7.1 Carbonic acid ionises in water according to the following balanced equation: H2CO3(aq) + H2O(ℓ) ⇌ HCO3⁻(aq) + H3O⁺(aq)
questions.text: Define an acid according to the Arrhenius theory.

questions.memo_answer: An acid is a substance that produces hydrogen ions (H⁺)/hydronium ions (H3O⁺) when it dissolves in water.

questions.text: FORMULAE of the TWO substances that can act as an ampholyte

questions.text: Balanced equation between carbonic acid and sodium hydroxide (NaOH)
questions.topic: Acids and bases
questions.memo_answer: H2CO3 + 2 NaOH → Na2CO3 + 2 H2O (1 mark reactants, 1 mark products, 1 mark balancing)

questions.context: 7.2 2 g of NaOH is dissolved in water to make a 100 cm3 solution. Calculate the:
questions.text: Concentration of NaOH
questions.topic: Acids and bases
questions.memo_answer:
OPTION 1: c = m / MV = 2 / (40)(0,1) = 0,5 mol·dm⁻³
OPTION 2: n = m / M = 2 / 40 = 0,05 mol; c = n / V = 0,05 / 0,1 = 0,5 mol·dm⁻³

questions.text: pH of NaOH
questions.topic: Acids and bases
questions.memo_answer:
OPTION 1: NaOH → Na⁺ + OH⁻, [OH⁻] = [NaOH] = 0,5 mol·dm⁻³
[OH⁻][H3O⁺] = 1 x 10⁻¹⁴: [H3O⁺](0,5) = 1 x 10⁻¹⁴, [H3O⁺] = 2 x 10⁻¹⁴ mol·dm⁻³
pH = -log[H3O⁺] = -log(2 x 10⁻¹⁴) = 13,70
OPTION 2: pOH = -log[OH⁻] = -log(0,5) = 0,30; pH + pOH = 14; pH = 13,70

questions.context: 7.3 5 g of impure magnesium carbonate (MgCO3) is added to 9,033 x 10²² molecules of hydrochloric acid (HCℓ). The balanced equation for the reaction that takes place is: MgCO3(s) + 2 HCℓ(aq) → MgCℓ2(aq) + CO2(g) + H2O(ℓ). The reaction is allowed to proceed until all the pure magnesium carbonate completely reacts. The excess hydrochloric acid is neutralised by adding 55 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution of concentration 0,8 mol·dm⁻³. The balanced equation for the neutralisation reaction is: HCℓ(aq) + NaOH(aq) → NaCℓ(aq) + H2O(ℓ). Calculate the:
questions.text: Initial number of moles of hydrochloric acid
questions.topic: Quantitative aspects: stoichiometry, limiting reagents and purity

questions.text: Percentage purity of magnesium carbonate
questions.topic: Quantitative aspects: stoichiometry, limiting reagents and purity
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 7.3.1.)
n(NaOH) = cV = 0,8 x 55/1 000 = 0,044 mol
NaOH : HCℓ = 1 : 1, n(HCℓ) excess = 0,044 mol
n(HCℓ) reacted with MgCO3 = 0,15 - 0,044 = 0,106 mol
HCℓ : MgCO3 = 2 : 1, n(MgCO3) = 0,053 mol
m = nM = 0,053 x 84 = 4,452 g
% purity = pure mass / sample mass x 100% = 4,452 / 5 x 100% = 89,04%

questions.context: QUESTION 8 (Start on a new page.) 8.1 A solution of nickel(II) nitrate is placed in a zinc container. It was observed, after some time, that a chemical reaction has taken place. The net ionic equation is: Zn(s) + Ni²⁺(aq) ⇌ Zn²⁺(aq) + Ni(s)
questions.text: Explain the term redox reaction.
questions.topic: Redox reactions and oxidation numbers
questions.memo_answer:
A redox is a reaction that involves an electron transfer.
OR
It is a reaction that always involve changes in oxidation numbers.

questions.text: Which ONE of Zn or Ni2+ is the oxidising agent? Explain the answer by referring to the oxidation numbers.
questions.topic: Redox reactions and oxidation numbers
questions.memo_answer:
Ni²⁺
Its oxidation number decreases from +2 to 0.

questions.text: Give a reason why the nitrate ion (NO3–) is not written in the net ionic equation above.
questions.topic: Redox reactions and oxidation numbers
questions.memo_answer: The nitrate ion (NO3⁻) is a spectator ion / undergoes no change in its oxidation state.

questions.context: 8.2 The reaction between dichromate ions (Cr2O7²⁻) and tin(II) ions (Sn²⁺) in an acid medium is given below: Cr2O7²⁻ + Sn²⁺ + H⁺ → Cr³⁺ + Sn⁴⁺ + H2O(ℓ)

questions.memo_answer: Cr2O7²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H2O

questions.memo_answer:
Sn²⁺ → Sn⁴⁺ + 2e⁻ (x 3)
Cr2O7²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H2O
